cases.sentence: Он хотел сказать, что напрасно Иван высоко подтянул чересседельню, но это было похоже на упрек, а ему хотелось ___.
cases.explain: «любовного разговора» — the genitive here marks possession, absence, or quantity.
cases.translation: Pulling the stiff rein and holding in the good horse that snorted with impatience and seemed begging to be let go, Levin looked round at Ivan sitting beside him, not knowing what to do with his unoccupied hand, continually pressing down his shirt as it puffed out, and he tried to find something to start a conversation about with him. He would have said that Ivan had pulled the saddle-girth up too high, but that was like blame, and he longed for friendly, warm talk. Nothing else occurred to him.

cases.explain: «неприятный человек» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.
cases.translation: “Oh, I hope it’s not a tiresome person!” thought Levin.

cases.sentence: Только загнув за поворот дороги и увидав шедших навстречу, Левин узнал Катавасова в ___, шедшего, точно так размахивая руками, как представляла Таня.
cases.explain: «соломенной шляпе» — after the preposition «в», for location or topic.
cases.translation: As soon as he turned, at a bend in the road, and saw the party coming, Levin recognized Katavasov in a straw hat, walking along swinging his arms just as Tanya had shown him. Katavasov was very fond of discussing metaphysics, having derived his notions from natural science writers who had never studied metaphysics, and in Moscow Levin had had many arguments with him of late.

cases.sentence: При этих словах глаза братьев встретились, и Левин, несмотря на всегдашнее и теперь особенно сильное в нем желание быть в дружеских и, главное, ___ с братом, почувствовал, что ему неловко смотреть на него.
cases.explain: «простых отношениях» — the prepositional is used only after a preposition, for location or topic.
cases.translation: At these words the brothers’ eyes met, and Levin, in spite of the desire he always had, stronger than ever just now, to be on affectionate and still more open terms with his brother, felt an awkwardness in looking at him. He dropped his eyes and did not know what to say.

cases.sentence: – Никто не занят этим, и я менее других, – сказал он. – Посмотрите, Дарья Александровна, будет дождик, – прибавил он, указывая зонтиком на показавшиеся над макушами осин ___.
cases.explain: «белые тучки» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.
cases.translation: “No one is interested in that now, and I less than anyone,” he said. “Just look, Darya Alexandrovna, we shall have a shower,” he added, pointing with a sunshade at the white rain clouds that showed above the aspen treetops.

cases.sentence: Стараясь делать как можно меньше ___ и прислушиваясь к пролетавшим все чаще и чаще мимо него пчелам, он дошел по тропинке до избы.
cases.explain: «быстрых движений» — the genitive here marks possession, absence, or quantity.
cases.translation: Trying to make his movements as deliberate as possible, and listening to the bees that buzzed more and more frequently past him, he walked along the little path to the hut. In the very entry one bee hummed angrily, caught in his beard, but he carefully extricated it. Going into the shady outer room, he took down from the wall his veil, that hung on a peg, and putting it on, and thrusting his hands into his pockets, he went into the fenced-in bee-garden, where there stood in the midst of a closely mown space in regular rows, fastened with bast on posts, all the hives he knew so well, the old stocks, each with its own history, and along the fences the younger swarms hived that year. In front of the openings of the hives, it made his eyes giddy to watch the bees and drones whirling round and round about the same spot, while among them the working bees flew in and out with spoils or in search of them, always in the same direction into the wood to the flowering lime trees and back to the hives.

cases.sentence: У ___ одна пчела завизжала, запутавшись ему в бороду, но он осторожно выпростал ее.
cases.explain: «самых сеней» — the genitive here marks possession, absence, or quantity.

cases.sentence: «Неужели это было только ___, и оно пройдет, не оставив следа?» – подумал он.
cases.explain: «минутное настроение» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.
cases.translation: “Can it have been only a momentary mood, and will it pass and leave no trace?” he thought. But the same instant, going back to his mood, he felt with delight that something new and important had happened to him. Real life had only for a time overcast the spiritual peace he had found, but it was still untouched within him.

cases.sentence: Как, несмотря на пчел, ___ была вся цела в нем, так и цела была вновь созданная им его духовная сила.
cases.explain: «телесная сила» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.
cases.translation: Just as the bees, whirling round him, now menacing him and distracting his attention, prevented him from enjoying complete physical peace, forced him to restrain his movements to avoid them, so had the petty cares that had swarmed about him from the moment he got into the trap restricted his spiritual freedom; but that lasted only so long as he was among them. Just as his bodily strength was still unaffected, in spite of the bees, so too was the spiritual strength that he had just become aware of.

cases.sentence: Как, несмотря на пчел, телесная сила была вся цела в нем, так и цела была вновь созданная им его ___.
